bulletins.title: Health Insurance and Medicare Open Enrollment Impersonation
bulletins.summary: During Open Enrollment, scammers use deceptive online ads and unsolicited calls posing as Medicare or ACA Marketplace representatives. Fraudsters claim that coverage will lapse or cards must be re-issued, pressing victims to verify numbers or pay immediate enrollment fees.
phrases: update your health insurance information immediately

bulletins.title: Social Engineering Calls Intercepting One-Time Passcodes
bulletins.summary: Fraudsters initiate unauthorized logins to target accounts and immediately contact the victim by phone or text claiming to be bank security or service representatives. They create false urgency around unauthorized activity and instruct the victim to read back the verification code, completing an account takeover.
phrases: read back the one time passcode
security representative calling about your account
verify the code we just sent
temporary authorization code to verify identity
confirm the six digit security code
passcode sent to stop unauthorized access

bulletins.title: Urgent Impersonation and AI Voice Cloning Schemes
bulletins.summary: Callers deploy urgency and emotional pressure, increasingly incorporating AI-cloned voices to impersonate distressed family members, bank fraud investigators, or law enforcement. Victims are told an account has been compromised or a loved one faces arrest, demanding immediate funds or card handovers.
phrases: your bank account has been compromised
loved one is in trouble need bail
transfer money to protect your funds

gemini_context_snippet: Active phone scams emphasize social engineering to intercept one-time passcodes under the guise of fraud prevention, and urgent impersonation calls utilizing AI voice cloning to fake family crises or bank freezes. In addition, open enrollment season brings deceptive calls claiming Medicare or Marketplace coverage requires immediate verification or card fees.
